George Santayana (1863-1952) was a Spanish-American philosopher, essayist, poet, and novelist. Born in Madrid, he was educated in the United States and spent much of his career teaching at Harvard University. Santayana is best known for his works on philosophy, aesthetics, and culture, including The Life of Reason. He emphasized the importance of critical thinking and intellectual independence. Though deeply influenced by classical philosophy, he maintained a skeptical and naturalistic outlook. Later in life, he returned to Europe, living in Italy until his death. His writings continue to influence modern thought and education.

Leo Tolstoy (1828-1910) was a renowned Russian novelist, philosopher, and social reformer, widely regarded as one of the greatest writers in world literature. He is best known for his epic novels War and Peace and Anna Karenina, which explore human emotions, society, and morality. Born into aristocratic family, Tolstoy later adopted a simple, spiritual lifestyle and promoted nonviolence and truth. His ideas influenced figures like Mahatma Gandhi. Through his works and philosophy, Tolstoy left a lasting impact on literature, ethics, and social thought worldwide.

 - Friedrich Nietzsche
